However, the further development of CTDE faces two key challenges. First, agents struggle to autonomously assess the relevance of input information for cooperative tasks, impairing their decision-making abilities. Second, in communication-limited scenarios with partial observability, agents are unable to access global information, restricting their ability to collaborate effectively from a global perspective. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel cooperative MARL framework based on information selection and tacit learning. In this framework, agents gradually develop implicit coordination during training, enabling them to infer the cooperative behavior of others in a discrete space without communication, relying solely on local information. Moreover, we integrate gating and selection mechanisms, allowing agents to adaptively filter information based on environmental changes, thereby enhancing their decision-making capabilities. payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=autonomous+problem+selection+information+gain+active+learning+uninstructed+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.65109/euke2930\", \"title\": [\"Tacit Learning with Adaptive Information Selection for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>In multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) framework has gained widespread adoption due to its strong performance. However, the further development of CTDE faces two key challenges. First, agents struggle to autonomously assess the relevance of input information for cooperative tasks, impairing their decision-making abilities. Second, in communication-limited scenarios with partial observability, agents are unable to access global information, restricting their ability to collaborate effectively from a global perspective. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel cooperative MARL framework based on information selection and tacit learning. In this framework, agents gradually develop implicit coordination during training, enabling them to infer the cooperative behavior of others in a discrete space without communication, relying solely on local information. Moreover, we integrate gating and selection mechanisms, allowing agents to adaptively filter information based on environmental changes, thereby enhancing their decision-making capabilities. Experiments on popular MARL benchmarks show that our framework can be seamlessly integrated with state-of-the-art algorithms, leading to significant performance improvements.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/euke2930\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 5, 28]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.31224/5919\", \"title\": [\"Active Dreaming Memory: Biologically-Inspired Episodic Consolidation for Lifelong Learning in Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) often suffer from catastrophic forgetting and lack temporal continuity. We present Active Dreaming Memory (ADM), a biologically-inspired dual-store memory system that enables agents to learn from execution failures without fine-tuning. Our key innovation is a counterfactual verification mechanism that validates candidate rules through synthetic scenario simulation before committing them to long-term memory. Experiments across six diverse domains demonstrate that ADM improves first-episode learning efficiency by 2× and achieves 83% success rate, significantly outperforming Reflexion, MemGPT, and Self-RAG. Catastrophic forgetting stress tests show 95% retention after 500 episodes. Theoretical analysis proves bounded forgetting guarantees and logarithmic memory growth. We release open-source code to support reproducible lifelong learning research.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31224/5919\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 3]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7557158\", \"title\": [\"Active Learning for Fuzzy Clustering: Robust Gain, Pairwise Selection, and Empirical Redundancy Diagnostics\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Active learning for fuzzy clustering must assess the benefit of a label before that label is observed. We study a reference soft-label entropy change, an ideal Kullback-Leibler robust expectation and a pairwise diversity selector. Corrected derivations give curvature and sampling bounds, an entropic dual, an oscillation-based robustness gap, and exact submodularity of a modular gain minus a nonnegative pairwise penalty; monotone greedy guarantees require additional conditions. An online analysis separates predictable regret bias from centered martingale fluctuations and gives a bounded-score worst-case inequality, without asserting a universal misspecification floor or vanishing regret. Gaussian moment matching is treated as an entropy-deficit diagnostic rather than a certified mutual-information approximation. The complete archived study on 13 datasets and 16 method configurations retains all supporting evidence and shows dataset-dependent effects of cross-block redundancy. Auditing reveals implementation differences and ineffective sensitivity switches, so the retained results describe the recorded heuristic and do not validate the corrected ideal formulation. We report these limits explicitly and identify the corrections and reruns needed for a reliable comparison.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7557158\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7557159\", \"title\": [\"Active Learning for Fuzzy Clustering: Robust Gain, Pairwise Selection, and Empirical Redundancy Diagnostics\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Active learning for fuzzy clustering must assess the benefit of a label before that label is observed. We study a reference soft-label entropy change, an ideal Kullback-Leibler robust expectation and a pairwise diversity selector. Corrected derivations give curvature and sampling bounds, an entropic dual, an oscillation-based robustness gap, and exact submodularity of a modular gain minus a nonnegative pairwise penalty; monotone greedy guarantees require additional conditions. An online analysis separates predictable regret bias from centered martingale fluctuations and gives a bounded-score worst-case inequality, without asserting a universal misspecification floor or vanishing regret. Gaussian moment matching is treated as an entropy-deficit diagnostic rather than a certified mutualinformation approximation. The complete archived study on 13 datasets and 16 method configurations retains all supporting evidence and shows dataset-dependent effects of cross-block redundancy. Auditing reveals implementation differences and ineffective sensitivity switches, so the retained results describe the recorded heuristic and do not validate the corrected ideal formulation. We report these limits explicitly and identify the corrections and reruns needed for a reliable comparison.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7557159\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "cd6df64d7f6d9bcd5633e6c470854642094c0466f4d0d496b5949bf2221cc21b", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_inquiry", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.65109/euke2930", "doi:10.31224/5919", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7557158", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7557159"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.65109/euke2930", "https://doi.org/10.31224/5919", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7557158", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7557159"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
